statement: Let $g(x)=\\frac{e^{x}-e^{-x}}{2}$ (the hyperbolic sine) and $f(x)=\\ln(x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+1})$. (i) Show that $f(g(x))=x$ and $g(f(x))=x$. (ii) Deduce that $f$ and $g$ are inverses and find $f'(x)$.
solution: (i) $g(x)=\\sinh x$, and $f(g(x))=\\ln(\\sinh x+\\sqrt{\\sinh^{2}x+1})=\\ln(\\sinh x+\\cosh x)=\\ln(e^{x})=x$. For the reverse, set $u=x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+1}$ so $e^{f(x)}=u$ and $e^{-f(x)}=1/u=\\sqrt{x^{2}+1}-x$. Then $g(f(x))=\\sinh(f(x))=\\frac{u-1/u}{2}=\\frac{2x}{2}=x$. (ii) Hence $f$ and $g$ are mutual inverses, and $f'(x)=\\frac{1+\\frac{x}{\\sqrt{x^{2}+1}}}{x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+1}}=\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{x^{2}+1}}$.
